Personality: Bovan seems out of place in martial Sturgia. Compassionate by nature, he cannot bear to witness needless slaughter, a trait often viewed as weakness on the brutal battlefields of the north. Lacking reckless courage, he acts with extreme caution—even appearing somewhat timid—and prefers to control the situation from afar using his superior archery and reconnaissance skills rather than throwing himself into bloody melee. Taking little interest in political scheming and unremarkable in generosity, he maintains a gentle, retiring posture within a harsh political environment. When confronted with the domineering, cruel, and heavy-handed style of his clan leader Vashorki, this temperament leaves him appearing submissive as he tries to preserve himself while holding fast to the kindness in his heart. He is more like a hunter forced to take up arms than a warrior hungry for glory.
Background: Bovan hails from the prominent Vyroving clan of Sturgia as the son of Ratagost. As a noble of Ov Castle, he grew up in the shadow of boyars vying for power and profit. Although his clan chief Vashorki is notorious for cruelty and tyranny, Bovan never acquired that ruthless streak. Within the Grand Principality of Sturgia, which evolved from a loose confederation, the storm clouds of rebellion constantly hang over Grand Prince Raganvad's rule. While Bovan is sworn to Raganvad, he is more like a bystander drawn passively into the political vortex. Through fine guerrilla instincts and accurate archery, he holds a place of his own within the family, yet his innate compassion and aversion to conflict keep him searching—in a turbulent realm that prizes Nord martial force and hereditary royal power—for a way of life that fulfills his duties as a lord without betraying his conscience.
